title: An Annealing-based Quantum Neural Network with Discrete Wavelet Transforms for Enhanced Air Pollution Nowcasting
authors: Otto Menegasso Pires, André Saimon, Daniela Herrmann, Prashant Kumar, Marcelo Moret, Erick Giovani Sperandio Nascimento
abstract: Air pollution poses a significant threat to public health, exacerbated by the rapid industrialization and urbanization of modern society. While traditional deep learning offers predictive capabilities, recent advancements in quantum machine learning (QML) present a compelling alternative. Here, we introduce a scalable hybrid framework that integrates variational quantum circuits with quantum annealing. Leveraging a neuromorphic quantum computing platform to transcend the qubit limitations of the NISQ era, we model particulate matter (PM$_{2.5}$) dynamics using high-density urban data from the UK. We demonstrate that our Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) exhibit an intrinsic resilience to input volatility, significantly outperforming classical baselines (MLP and LSTM) on raw, high-entropy environmental data. Furthermore, we successfully scaled the model to 172 qubits, observing a synergistic enhancement when coupled with wavelet decomposition that achieves state-of-the-art predictive fidelity. These findings establish a critical benchmark for quantum utility, proving that scalable, neuromorphic quantum machine learning can now address complex, non-linear real-world problems.
summary: This work proposes an annealing-based Quantum Neural Network (QNN) combined with Wavelet Transforms to forecast air pollution (PM2.5). By leveraging a neuromorphic quantum platform, the QNN demonstrates superior predictive accuracy compared to classical deep learning models on complex environmental data. This establishes a benchmark for applying scalable quantum machine learning to critical, non-linear real-world scientific challenges.
main_problem: The paper addresses the critical global health threat posed by air pollution, specifically forecasting fine particulate matter (PM2.5) concentrations (nowcasting).
main_result: The proposed Quantum Neural Network (QNN) framework significantly outperforms classical deep learning baselines (MLP, LSTM) on raw, high-entropy environmental data, achieving state-of-the-art predictive fidelity.
method: A hybrid framework integrating variational quantum circuits with quantum annealing is used, enhanced by Discrete Wavelet Transforms for feature decomposition.
model_or_system: The model is built on a neuromorphic quantum computing platform (DynexQML), encoding the problem into an energy minimization framework solved via quantum annealing to simulate a QNN structure.
key_observables: Normalized Mean Square Error (NMSE) and Pearson's R correlation coefficient are used to quantify predictive performance.
important_parameters: The model was successfully scaled and tested up to 172 qubits, with trainable parameters including variational angles ($	heta, \phi, \omega$) and model depth ($L$).
main_assumptions: The performance is demonstrated on an emulated platform, meaning true physical quantum advantage over noise and decoherence has not been validated.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the QNN structure (Feature Map and Ansatz) and time series comparisons showing QNN predictions versus classical models, including 95% prediction intervals.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the QNN architecture (encoding, ansatz, output), explains the quantum annealing mapping (circuit to QUBO), validates the method against classical models using statistical tests, and concludes with performance metrics and future work.
why_interesting: The application of quantum annealing to solve a complex, non-linear, real-world data problem like environmental forecasting provides a concrete, albeit simulated, testbed for quantum machine learning utility beyond abstract quantum chemistry simulations.
